content.text: Hungarian DominÃ³ (Block Game) is a strategic domino variant played with a Double-Six set. It is a 'block' game, meaning there is no drawing from a boneyard once play begins. Players must use the tiles in their hand to build a single linear chain, emphasizing hand management and blocking strategies to force opponents into passing their turns.
Dominoes arrived in Hungary in the 18th century. The 'Block' variant developed as a common social game in cafes, where fast play and simple scoring were preferred.

- 2 players: 12 tiles each (4 tiles remain out).
- 3 players: 8 tiles each (4 tiles remain out).
- 4 players: 6 tiles each (4 tiles remain out).

items.text: Double-Eight (Hungarian traditional): Play with a Double-8 set of 45 tiles. Deal: 2 players 21 each, 3 players 14 each, 4 players 10 each; three or five tiles remain out. Play is anticlockwise. Otherwise same block and scoring rules.
36-tile set: Remove the nine doubles from the Double-8 set; 36 tiles remain. Four players draw 8 tiles each, four tiles out of play. Otherwise same as Hungarian Block.

Buy-in (beszállás): When a player's penalty points reach 100 or more they may buy in to stay: their score is set to the highest score below 100 among others, and all players below 100 score one bonus tally mark. Game ends when a player reaches an agreed tally target (e.g. 10 marks) or is last survivor.
